title: AI-Assisted Debugging & Diagnostics
description: Master AI-augmented troubleshooting in .NET: diagnosing memory leaks, threadpool starvation, EF Core N+1 queries, unhandled async exceptions, and integrating LLMs with dotnet-dump, dotnet-trace, and OpenTelemetry.

data.text: The Modern AI Diagnostics Paradigm in .NET

Production debugging in enterprise .NET applications rarely fails due to a lack of data; it fails due to an overwhelming volume of disconnected telemetry. A production crash might generate gigabytes of memory dumps, millions of OpenTelemetry span logs, and deep nested stack traces. Using AI for debugging is not about pasting a raw error message into a chatbot and praying for a fix; it is a disciplined methodology for extracting diagnostic artifacts, feeding structured evidence to the LLM, generating verifiable hypotheses, and creating automated reproduction tests.

data.caption: Enterprise AI-Assisted Diagnostics & Resolution Pipeline
data.code:
flowchart TD
    A[Production Incident / Crash] --> B[Collect Artifacts: dotnet-dump, OTel Traces, Exception Logs]
    B --> C[Diagnostic Context Reduction: Extract Call Tree & Top 5 Stacks]
    C --> D[Feed Context to AI with Runtime Environment Constraints]
    D --> E[LLM Diagnostic Hypotheses & Ranked Culprits]
    E --> F[Generate Isolated Failing Unit / Integration Test]
    F -->|Test Fails to Reproduce| G[Refine Telemetry Context & Heap Root Analysis]
    G --> D
    F -->|Test Confirms Bug| H[Implement Targeted Hotfix]
    H --> I[Verify Fix Against Reproduction Suite & Deploy]

data.text: ThreadPool starvation is one of the most insidious bugs in .NET microservices. It typically occurs when asynchronous code is synchronously blocked using `.Result` or `.Wait()`, depleting worker threads during sudden traffic spikes. When diagnosing this, feeding raw thread dumps to an LLM without filtering can confuse the model. You must extract and format the active stack frames.

data.title: ThreadPool Starvation Call Stack Diagnosis
data.content: Here is a filtered stack trace from `dotnet-dump analyze` using the SOS command `~*e !clrstack`. We provide this to the AI alongside the offending method signature.

data.title: Why Sync-Over-Async Kills Production Systems
data.content: When a worker thread blocks on `.Result`, it remains idle while waiting for the completion thread. When hundreds of concurrent requests arrive, all ThreadPool threads become blocked. The runtime can only inject 1–2 new threads every 500ms, causing response latency to spike from 10ms to tens of seconds before catastrophic timeout cascades.

data.text: Memory Leak Diagnostics with dotnet-dump & SOS

Unmanaged event subscriptions and static cache roots are the top sources of managed memory leaks in long-running .NET processes. When memory climbs steadily in production, capture a process dump with `dotnet-dump collect -p <PID>` and analyze object counts.

data.caption: Diagnostic Tools, SOS Commands, and AI Prompt Strategy
rows: Top 5 classes with highest total byte size and instance counts
Prompt AI to examine root references (!gcroot) and identify event subscription leaks
Flame graph hot paths and top CPU-consuming methods
Prompt AI for algorithmic complexity (O(N^2) loops) and lock contention
OpenTelemetry Exception Telemetry / ILogger Structured Logs
Full exception tree including InnerException and AggregateException
Prompt AI to uncover async void boundary violations or unobserved Task exceptions
dotnet-trace or SQL Profiler / EF Core DebugView
Generated SQL logs with repetitive query patterns inside loop
Prompt AI to rewrite query using projection (.Select) or eager loading (.Include)

data.text: Reproducing the Bug with Automated Tests

The hallmark of an expert engineer using AI is not simply accepting the LLM's suggested fix; it is requiring the AI to write a reproduction unit test that fails before the fix is applied and passes after.

data.title: AI-Generated Memory Leak Reproduction Test
data.content: This test demonstrates using WeakReference to prove that an event handler was holding onto the subscriber, preventing Garbage Collection.

data.title: AI Debugging Production Protocol
items: Sanitize all PII, API tokens, and connection strings from stack traces and logs before prompting
Include exact .NET runtime version, OS architecture, and GC mode (Server vs Workstation)
Never paste raw multi-megabyte logs; extract the relevant 10-30 lines of call stack and error context
Ask AI for top 3 ranked hypotheses with specific falsification criteria for each
Require the LLM to write a failing xUnit/NUnit test that reproduces the bug before accepting any fix
Verify that the fix does not introduce regression in concurrency, latency, or memory consumption
Document the root cause and add defensive static analysis rules or lint checks to CI

data.title: Summary & Next Steps
points: AI debugging accelerates root-cause analysis when fed structured diagnostic evidence.
dotnet-dump and OpenTelemetry traces provide the necessary empirical ground truth.
Always pair AI diagnosis with reproduction testing (e.g., GC memory checks, async starvation mocks).
Modernize error handling to prevent sync-over-async and unobserved task exceptions.
data.takeaway: Empirical evidence is king in production diagnostics: use dotnet diagnostic tools to gather the truth, AI to brainstorm the hypotheses, and automated tests to verify the fix.
